padding_verdict.question: 78 of 254 target-side vbtable COMDATs are exactly ours + 4 trailing zeros. dtk splitter padding, or a real retail emission difference?
padding_verdict.verdict: PADDING, attributed to the vbtable by dtk's splitter.
padding_verdict.discriminator: dtk sizes a split symbol by the gap to the next thing it can name, so under the padding reading the tail must track the SUCCESSOR's alignment and under the emission reading it cannot. Tabulated over all 254 by `retail_map_fold_candidates.py --padding-evidence`; no exceptions.
padding_verdict.the_control: the 47. Their last word sits at addr % 8 == 4 and they are NOT padded, because the datum after them only wanted 4-byte alignment. An emitted terminator entry would be present in all 254 regardless of what follows.
corroboration: every ??_8 COMDAT we emit is IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_4BYTES (792/792), so the linker never pads a vbtable for the vbtable's own sake and any padding after one belongs to what follows
the target size histogram is 12:103, 8:96, 16:36, 24:10, 20:9 -- not the uniform '+1 terminator entry' shape a real emission difference would give
the 4 bytes are zero, and a vbtable entry of 0 would mean a virtual base at displacement 0 from the vbptr, which is degenerate

defects_found_and_fixed.impact: MSVC puts ??_7 at Value=4 behind the complete-object-locator pointer (5,220/5,220 of ours) and dtk puts it at 0 (2,863/2,863), so reading from 0 compared our 12-byte [??_R4 ptr][slot][slot] against the target's 8-byte [slot][slot] and called a matching vftable a content mismatch. Every ??_8 is at Value=0 on both sides, so the vbtable numbers are unaffected.

defects_found_and_fixed.what: objdiff-cli report cache does not key on objdiff.json's map_file
defects_found_and_fixed.impact: `report generate -o X.json` writes a sidecar X.cache and seeds the next run from it, keyed on hash_unit + hash_options. Re-running into the same -o path after only the ICF alias map changed returned 2224 hits and a report byte-identical to the baseline for a map with 340 more names in it -- a +143-function change measured as +0. build/373307D9/report.cache is the same sidecar for ninja's PROGRESS output and poisons a plain `report generate -p .` the same way. tools/none_guard.py was exposed in the direction that matters: a cached report cannot show a lost function, so it always says 'none is intact'.
defects_found_and_fixed.fixed_in: tools/none_guard.py now purges the sidecar and refuses to grade a report with any cache hit
